question: If \(b\ne d,\) the fractions \(\dfrac{ax+b}{cx+d}\) and \(\dfrac bd\) are unequal if:
solution:
The displayed fractions require \(d\ne0\) and \(cx+d\ne0\); work throughout on this domain. To decide when they are unequal, first determine when they are equal. Cross-multiplication gives
\[
\frac{ax+b}{cx+d}=\frac bd
\iff d(ax+b)=b(cx+d)
\iff x(ad-bc)=0.
\]
Under choice A, \(a=c=1\), so the last product becomes \(x(d-b)\). Both factors are nonzero because \(x\ne0\) and \(b\ne d\). Equality is therefore impossible.

The other choices give equality wherever the fractions are defined: in B both fractions are zero; in C and D the first fraction becomes \(b/d\); and in E the factor \(ad-bc\) is zero. Thus the required condition is choice A.
